messages.content: What did Dorothy say about living among the Mangaboos when the Wizard suggested fighting?
She would rather die there than live any longer among them.
What did the Wizard tell the children about it?
He would go along with whatever they decided, but they could not live long in the cavern.
What did the Wizard tell Jim about crossing the last stretch of the Valley of Voe?
He had to make a dash and run as fast as he could.
What did Jim say about his ability to dash?
He would try his best, but he was old and his dashing days were over.
What did Dorothy say about the fabric of her gown when the Braided Man tried to sell her rustles?
Her gown was not silk.
What did the Braided Man tell Dorothy about it?
The rustles would escape when the box opened whether she wore a silk dress or not.
What did the Wizard say about paying for the flutters?
He had no money with him.
What did the Braided Man want instead of money?
A blue hair-ribbon.
What did the Wizard say about the damage Jim did to the wooden Gargoyles?
He only knocked a few splinters from their noses and ears.
What did Dorothy say about retreating down the stairs?
She opposed going back because they would never get home that way and wanted to fight it out.
What did the Wizard ask the others to do when they were about to be sealed in by the Mangaboos?
He suggested jumping out and fighting.
What did the Wizard say about associating with strangers in the dragonettes’ cave?
They were a little particular about who they associated with.
